pr_title: Making drawer accesable for easy navigation
pr_body:
- [x] I carefully read the [contribution guidelines](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/HEAD/.github/CONTRIBUTING.md) and agree to them.

Fixes #3135
Closes #2358

Additions: 
1. Now Navigation is accessible from both MainFragment, VideoDetailFragment.
2. Added the "Home" tab to the drawer to reach home (MainFragment) easily.

I tested this rigorously and there are no bugs I can find. And, I find the app very easy to navigate now :)
This is the Debug-Apk for testing: [Debug-Apk](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1ii2awCyGs7hh8fZvvkeze_4kAQFE0w8u/view?usp=sharing) (Changed the package name for side by side install) 

ZIP Version of APK: [app-debug.zip](https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/files/4292429/app-debug.zip)

> Yeah, very true but can you tell me the distinction between the back and up button in play store when you are deep into apps how will you go home? why do we need two buttons doing the same thing?

They are not doing the same thing, test in your end these steps to see it:

- Open an app page.
- Navigate to multiple related apps.
- Click the up button.

You should be home, because that's what that button does, navigate a level up. It's subtle, but there _is_ a difference.

> That's because they have the bottom navigation. We have much handy side navigation bar, they have different scenario than ours, it's not very suitable to compare.

It's very suitable because they also have the same navigation view and it's enabled at all times, _even when you are deep navigating through items_, that's why I talked about that app.

###### Of course, doing the same thing that Play Store does isn't good just because Google does it, but because I think it makes sense (and you can find other other apps doing that now).

> It still preserved in the back button, the back button is almost exactly doing what the up button is doing, as it's mentioned in that link....

It's not the same, with the back button you'd have to keep pressing it multiple times. The up button is a _level_ upwards navigation.

Here's some relevant parts:
>> Upward navigation allows users to navigate one level upwards within a single app’s hierarchy, until the app’s home or top-level screen is reached. For example, the Up arrow in a top app bar is a form of upwards reverse navigation.

>> Clearly indicate child screens’ relationship with screens above them in the hierarchy. For example, if a user moves directly to a child screen in your app, they should be able to identify the parent screen to which they can navigate upward.

This was discussed before, the solution that we ended up with was:

https://github.com/TeamNewPipe/NewPipe/blob/d5c29bf1b540e8e9243651b6d43baa177884c29a/app/src/main/java/org/schabi/newpipe/MainActivity.java#L512-L542

> What is "Parent screen" can you please explain? which action?

Take in consideration that I mentioned the case where keeping the drawer icon would make sense.

Another way to call it would be "Home screen", the one that is visible when you open the app from a closed state. The action in this case would be the user pressing a button in said drawer.

Usually, it is used in apps that have a flat navigation, that is, there's no child screens, similar to how the bottom navigation bar does it (though in the case of the bottom navigation you'd still have to indicate to the user that they aren't in the "home screen" by showing the up button when they navigate away from home, again, how it's done in the Play Store).

> Which one is it mate? you like it or you don't like it? I don't understand xD

>> The drawer available from every screen is very useful, I thought about adding it as well.
>>
>>>>>>> ### About the up button:
>>
>> IMO, it should be kept as it is, some reasons why:

xDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDDD

----

Even if we disagree about the up button behavior, what the icon represents it's what is important. Just keep it.

> Up button will take you to home, I think drawer gives more functionality.

That's the thing. The up button is not 'just another home button' or a duplicate of the back button. It goes one level up in the app screen hierarchy. For example, if you go to the search fragment, then open a search result, tapping the up button takes you one level up to the search fragment, and _not_ the home screen, which needs another tap of the button.

> I think the up buttton should be removed and hamburger reintroduced as most android devices have back buttons on them that have the same function as up buttons in app UI.

Another thing to note here is that you can open several further videos after that first one, but the up button will _still_ take you to the search fragment, showing how it's different from the OS back button.

Personally, I don't use it. But I can imagine a situation where someone has been opening several videos in a chain, reached somewhere unrelated, and has forgotten the search term. Having to go back all the way with the OS back button would be irritating, if the up button were not there anymore.

issue_context.title: Make drawer accessible from every activity
issue_context.body:
Probably related to #3128, could you add other options like downloads to (now-gone) app bar?
IMO this can make navigation bit faster.

Or a potentially better way, adding an option to the settings to return UI back to pre-0.18.3 design?
comments: Apparently it was a bad idea to remove menus from everywhere, they should probably be reintroduced. The only place that should stay without menus is the main page, where the drawer is openable. What do you think @TobiGr @opusforlife2 @gillhash

I still maintain that having the drawer instead of the 3 dot menu everywhere except a few screens is the better way to go. It gives the user immediate access to a wider variety of menus and options.

Why should the user have to back out all the way to the home screen if they feel like having a glance at their Bookmarked Playlists, for example?
Adding the drawer would force us to remove the back button though
@Stypox: No, look at how you could still access the drawer by swiping at for example the 'My apps & games' screen in the Play Store
@opusforlife2 my bad, I missed that comment ;-)
Hey everyone, I made a PR addressing this can you please take a look :)
Closing this issue as this doesn't apply to 0.20.x versions (the entire top bar is gone). I'll look after this again if the old UI resurfaces or the devs decided to reimplement the top bar again.
